source.dataset_title: Red Fox (Vulpes vulpes) in UK wet grasslands

estimand: Day-balanced observed 2D geographic utilization-distribution overlap O_ij=sum_c min(p_i(c),p_j(c)); per site × reference deployment year × original GPS calendar month; each animal-day has equal weight, each fix within day equal weight. Individual >=40 fixes on >=5 tracking days per month, dyad >=3 shared tracked dates. Fixed source-mean-latitude equirectangular grid. This is X not R or independently observed E/T. Paired month units reuse animals and cannot be interpreted as independent replicates.
known_confounders: Site and original sampling years are completely confounded (Britford 2016–17, Somerley 2018–19); this is not a causal site contrast

Source published study already documents site differences in population density, management, food subsidies and home-range scales; this X contrast is an original quantitative pilot, not by itself new ecology
Individuals in source are adults; individual IDs reused across multiple deployments but not across study years/sites, and animal-day records cannot be treated as independent pairs
GPS accuracy/horizontal-dilution/sampling-gap spatial cell support needs robust sensitivity checks
1-km cell overlap is not simultaneous physical encounters or measured dietary resource use
R conditional movement signatures, independently measured ecological resources E and temporal sharing T were not estimated
intended_next: Within-source site-year same-month common 1km/2km location and time-gap opportunity gate before leave-day-out movement-mode identity R. If common cells/effort insufficient, structural stop not negative identity.
